input: Practice mindfulness meditation for ten minutes daily

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The time of day and physical setting (morning at home, lunch break at work, etc.) shapes the routine design and what reminders or environment cues will actually work.
Mindfulness meditation covers many styles (breath focus, body scan, loving-kindness, guided, silent). Knowing which type the user wants determines the specific practice to build around.
Whether this is purely solo or involves an accountability partner, a group, or a teacher changes the social scaffolding and support structure of the plan.
The user's prior experience level determines where to start — a complete beginner needs guided resources, while someone experienced just needs a consistency system.
Whether the user wants to use an app, a timer, a guided audio track, or nothing at all determines the tools and setup steps required.
Understanding what outcome 'done well' looks like (stress reduction, better focus, emotional regulation, spiritual growth) allows the plan to track meaningful progress markers.
Some people need strict scheduling and reminders to stick to habits; others prefer flexibility. This determines how the daily trigger and habit loop should be structured.

gold.taskDescription: The user wants to build a consistent habit of practising mindfulness meditation for ten minutes every day.

questions.title: What time of day do you plan to meditate?
questions.description: Knowing the preferred time slot (morning, midday, evening) and the setting (bedroom, office, outdoors) allows the plan to design a realistic, location-anchored routine.

questions.title: Which style of meditation do you want to practise?
questions.description: Identifying the preferred style — such as breath-focused, body scan, loving-kindness, or open awareness — determines the exact practice to follow each session.

questions.title: How experienced are you with meditation right now?
questions.description: Experience level (complete beginner, occasional practitioner, or regular meditator) dictates whether the plan needs introductory guidance, technique refinement, or just a consistency structure.

questions.title: What tool or resource do you want to use for sessions?
questions.description: Whether the user prefers a guided app (Headspace, Calm, Insight Timer), a simple phone timer, or unassisted silence determines the setup and onboarding steps.

questions.title: Do you want to practise alone or with accountability from someone?
questions.description: Knowing whether the user wants a solo habit versus a partner check-in, group, or teacher shapes the social support layer of the plan.

questions.title: What main benefit are you hoping to gain from this habit?
questions.description: The primary goal — reducing stress, improving focus, managing emotions, or spiritual development — allows the plan to define meaningful progress markers and keep motivation aligned.

questions.title: Do you prefer a fixed daily schedule or flexible timing?
questions.description: Understanding whether the user thrives with a strict daily trigger (same time every day) or needs flexibility determines how reminders and habit cues should be structured.
